The correct answer is __**Kei Nishikori**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kei Nishikori**, the veteran tennis star from **Japan**, etched his name in history by becoming the **first Asian male** player to reach the milestone of **450 career wins** on the **ATP Tour** by **April 2025**.
 
• This achievement highlights his longevity and dominance in professional tennis, particularly as he remains the most successful male singles player representing an Asian nation in the Open Era.
 
• The milestone was reached following a determined comeback from a series of debilitating **injuries**, including **hip surgery** in **2022** and subsequent **knee** and **ankle** issues that kept him out of consistent competition for much of **2023** and **2024**.
 
• Nishikori's **450th victory** serves as a testament to his resilience, further extending his record lead over other notable Asian players like **Vijay Amritraj** and **Paradorn Srichaphan**.
 
• Known for his exceptional **return of serve** and **backhand down the line**, Nishikori has maintained a high winning percentage throughout his career, which began professionally in **2007**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kei Nishikori (Japan):**
 
 
• Born on **December 29, 1989**, in **Shimane, Japan**, he moved to the **United States** at age 14 to train at the **IMG Academy**.
 
• He reached a career-high ranking of **World No. 4** in **March 2015** and became the first Asian-born man to reach a **Grand Slam singles final** at the **2014 US Open**.
 
• He has won **12 ATP singles titles** and earned an **Olympic Bronze Medal** for Japan at the **2016 Rio Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Yuki Bhambri (India):**
 
 
• A former **Junior World No. 1** and winner of the **2009 Australian Open Junior** championship.
 
• While a top-tier talent for India, his singles career faced interruptions due to **tendonitis**. In recent years, he has successfully transitioned to the **ATP Doubles** circuit, achieving a top 50 ranking. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect regarding the 450 singles wins.***
 
 
 
• **Prajnesh Gunneswaran (India):**
 
 
• He reached a career-high ranking of **75** in **2019** and has been a key player for India in the **Davis Cup**.
 
• His career wins at the ATP main draw level are far below the 450 mark compared to Nishikori. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Somdev Devvarman (India):**
 
 
• A **three-time NCAA finalist** and **two-time champion**, he is one of India's most decorated collegiate and professional players.
 
• He won **Gold Medals** at both the **Commonwealth Games** and **Asian Games** in **2010** before retiring in **2017**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Winning Percentage:** Nishikori is famously ranked among the all-time leaders in **winning percentage in fifth sets**, showcasing his mental toughness in long matches.
 
• **Project 45:** Early in his career, he was nicknamed "Project 45" as he aimed to beat the record of **Shuzo Matsuoka**, who was the highest-ranked Japanese male player at **World No. 46**. Nishikori surpassed this in **2011**.
 
• **ATP Milestone Context:** Reaching **450 wins** puts a player in an elite bracket of the **ATP Tour**, usually occupied by Grand Slam champions and consistent Top 10 mainstays over a decade-long span.

questions.question: According to the UN Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025, what is India’s SDG Index Rank and Score?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rank 99 with score 66.95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025**, **India** has achieved a global **Rank of 99**.
 
• The country has attained an overall **SDG Index Score of 66.95**, which indicates its cumulative progress toward achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report** is an annual global assessment that tracks the performance of all **193 UN Member States** on the **SDGs**.
 
• The report is produced by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which has been operating since **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** and is led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs**.
 
• The **SDG Index score** can be interpreted as the percentage of **SDG achievement**; a score of **66.95** suggests India is roughly **67%** of the way to the optimal target (100).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDGs**, also known as the **Global Goals**, were adopted by the **United Nations** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty and protect the planet by **2030**.
 
• There are **17 specific goals**, including **SDG 1 (No Poverty)**, **SDG 5 (Gender Equality)**, and **SDG 13 (Climate Action)**.
 
 
 
• **The Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• This **organisation** mobilizes scientific and technical expertise from academia, civil society, and the private sector to support practical problem-solving for **sustainable development**.
 
• The **SDR** is the first worldwide study to assess where each country stands with regard to achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals**.
 
 
 
• **India's Domestic Monitoring:**
 
 
• In **India**, the **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for overseeing the implementation of **SDGs**.
 
• It releases the **SDG India Index** annually to track the progress of **States** and **Union Territories**, ensuring competitive federalism in achieving **global targets**.
 
 
 
• **Global Leaders:**
 
 
• Historically, **Nordic countries** such as **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** consistently rank at the top of the **SDG Index** due to robust social safety nets and environmental policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Decade of Action:** The **United Nations** has termed the period from **2020 to 2030** as the **Decade of Action**, urging all countries to accelerate sustainable solutions to all the world’s biggest challenges.
 
• **Performance Indicators:** The **SDG Index** uses a wide range of data points, including **health outcomes**, **economic growth**, **educational attainment**, and **carbon emissions**, to provide a holistic view of national development.
 
• **SDR 2025 Context:** The **2025 report** emphasizes the need for **International Financial Architecture** reform to provide **developing nations** with the necessary **liquidity** and **investment** to reach the **2030 goals**.

questions.question: Where was the 2025 Senior National Table Tennis Championships held?

options.text: Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Indoor Stadium, Surat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Indoor Stadium, Surat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **86th Senior National Table Tennis Championships** were scheduled to be held at the **Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Indoor Stadium** in **Surat**, **Gujarat** in **January 2025**.
 
• This event is the premier domestic competition organized by the **Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI)**, featuring the highest level of competition for Indian paddlers.
 
• The choice of **Surat** as the host city underscores **Gujarat’s** status as a growing sports hub in India, having successfully hosted major events like the **36th National Games** and previous editions of the national championships.
 
• The tournament serves as a crucial platform for players to improve their national rankings and secure spots in the national squad for international events like the **ITTF World Championships** and **Asian Games**.
 
• The competition features top-tier athletes including Olympic participants and Commonwealth Games medalists such as **Achanta Sharath Kamal**, **Manika Batra**, and **Sreeja Akula**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Indoor Stadium**:
 
 
• Located in the **Ghod Dod Road** area of **Surat**, it is a state-of-the-art indoor arena inaugurated in **1998**.
 
• It was the first of its kind in **Western India** to be fully air-conditioned and has a seating capacity of approximately **7,000** spectators.
 
• The stadium frequently hosts diverse events ranging from **badminton**, **volleyball**, and **table tennis** to cultural programs and international conventions.
 
 
 
• **Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI)**:
 
 
• Established in **1926**, it is the governing body for table tennis in India and is a founder member of the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it oversees the development of the sport through various age-category nationals and the **Ultimate Table Tennis (UTT)** league.
 
 
 
• **Key Players in Indian Table Tennis**:
 
 
• **Achanta Sharath Kamal**: A legendary figure who holds the record for the most **Senior National titles (10)** and was awarded the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** in **2022**.
 
• **Manika Batra**: The first Indian woman to win a common-wealth individual gold in table tennis and a recipient of the **Arjuna Award** and **Khel Ratna**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Structure**:
 
 
• The Senior Nationals typically include **Men's Singles**, **Women's Singles**, **Men's Doubles**, **Women's Doubles**, and **Mixed Doubles** events.
 
• It also includes **Inter-State Team Championships** where various states and institutional teams like **Petroleum Sports Promotion Board (PSPB)** and **Railways (RSPB)** compete for top honors.
